edge_explainer.market_believes: Booz Allen is the government-services name most exposed to DOGE-era civilian cuts: revenue fell 6% this year, its consulting-heavy civil business is shrinking ~20-28%, FY27 EPS is guided DOWN, Treasury very publicly fired it, and the historical premium multiple deserved to compress.
edge_explainer.we_believe: Most of that is honestly-disclosed cyclical civil weakness in only ~29% of the book — offset by a defense segment (54%) that GREW, resilient intel, and a $800M+ AI business growing 30%. Total revenue is guided to STABILIZE in FY27, book-to-bill is a healthy 1.1x with record backlog, the Treasury cancellation is 0.04% of revenue, and the balance sheet funds an ~11% shareholder yield. It is a fairly-valued quality franchise, not a falling knife.
edge_explainer.why_no_edge: Our 3-scenario probability-weighted fair value lands exactly at the $62 price. The market is pricing stabilization correctly. There is nothing mispriced to arbitrage — it is fair-carry (RP_FAIR), not edge.
edge_explainer.why_we_harvest_anyway: The position is a small 50-share lot at a ~$880 loss. Harvesting banks a real tax benefit against our large 2026 winners (aligned with the tax-asymmetry plan), gives up a slightly-negative-EV Jul-28 catalyst, and does not sacrifice edge (there is none). We can re-source government-services carry after the wash window via BAH itself or a post-gate MMS, whichever earns it.
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: If the Jul-28 print shows the DEFENSE segment going negative organic and the FY27 revenue guide gets CUT below $11.2B, then the civil weakness has spread to the anchor and the 'contained + offset' read is wrong — BAH is then a structural short, not a fair-carry hold, and re-entry is off.
